sections.html:
Sarpy County is the smallest Nebraska county by area and the third largest by population. It covers 247.5 square miles between the Missouri River on the east and the Platte River on the south and west, and it belongs to the Omaha-Council Bluffs metropolitan area, with Douglas County to the north. Papillion is the county seat, Bellevue is the biggest city, and Gretna, La Vista and Springfield are the other cities.

The 2020 census counted 190,604 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 208,303. The 2024 estimate shows 77,583 households, 2.63 persons per household and median household income of $101,316. Papillion alone had 24,159 residents in 2020.

Offutt Air Force Base sits just south of Bellevue and is home to U.S. Strategic Command. Military families move on orders, so a house sometimes has to sell on a fixed timeline. In that spot, compare how long each way of selling is likely to take, not just the price.

sections.h2: Why Sarpy tax dates are earlier
sections.html:
Sarpy has more than 100,000 residents, so it follows the larger-county schedule in Nebraska Statute 77-204. The first half is delinquent April 1 and the second half August 1, rather than the May 1 and September 1 dates used in smaller counties. The first installment is due the day before the April date, at the Treasurer's Office.

An April delinquency can surprise a seller who is planning around the May date common in the rest of the state. If you plan to sell in spring, ask the treasurer what is already due.

sections.h2: How a Sarpy County valuation protest works
sections.html:
The assessor certifies new values on or before June 1 and mails a Notice of Valuation Change only to owners whose value changed. Value is market value as of January 1, worked out by mass appraisal using cost, income and sales comparison approaches. Agricultural land is assessed at 75 percent of market value under the Nebraska Constitution.

Protest Form 422 can be filed only from June 1 to June 30. The County Clerk takes it online or by mail, or in person, until 4:45 p.m. on June 30, and a deadline that lands on a weekend moves to the next business day. Forms postmarked or received before June 1 are returned. Include your reasons, a description of the property, your signature, the date and the parcel number, and cross out personal data, because protests are public records.

Present evidence that the assessor valued the property above market or out of line with similar properties. The board can hire independent appraisers as referees. Under Statute 77-1502, owners in counties over 100,000 may meet in person with the board or a referee, and those counties may extend the hearing window from July 25 to August 10.

A ruling by the Board of Equalization can be appealed to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission at 301 Centennial Mall S. in Lincoln, phone 402-471-2842. The deadline is August 24, or September 10 when the county extended its hearings.

The Treasurer publishes the delinquent tax list in the Omaha Daily Record, and the county keeps a Tax Sale Information page. Buyers at a tax sale purchase the delinquent amount, and Nebraska law (statutes 77-1801 to 77-1941) governs what happens if the owner does not redeem.

Phone the treasurer for a payoff figure before any closing date is set. A balance that looks small on paper can still hold up a closing if the title company finds it late.

Papillion-La Vista Public Schools (District 27), Bellevue Public Schools (District 1) and Gretna Public Schools (District 37) serve most of the county. Millard Public Schools and Omaha Public Schools reach into it, along with Springfield Platteview Community Schools, Louisville Public Schools and Ashland-Greenwood Public Schools.

With this many overlapping districts, two houses a block apart can be billed by different districts and owe different totals. Read the tax district code on your statement before comparing.

The title company collects the tax payoff from your proceeds, and you pay the documentary stamp tax through the register of deeds. The rate is $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026, and Form 521 is filed with the deed.

Houses with deferred repairs, liens or tax problems are the ones owners struggle to sell the usual way. If a house in Bellevue, Papillion, La Vista, Gretna or Springfield needs work you do not want to pay for, send us the address and we will explain what an as-is cash sale would look like.

faqs.q: When are Sarpy County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: The first half is delinquent April 1 and the second half August 1, because Sarpy has more than 100,000 residents.

faqs.q: When can I file a Sarpy County valuation protest?
faqs.a: Only from June 1 to June 30. Forms received before June 1 are returned, and the deadline is 4:45 p.m. on June 30 at the County Clerk's office.

faqs.q: Where is the Sarpy County Treasurer?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's Office is at 1102 E. 1st Street in Papillion, and the phone is 402-593-2143.

faqs.q: Can I appeal a Sarpy County Board of Equalization decision?
faqs.a: Yes, to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission in Lincoln, phone 402-471-2842, by August 24, or September 10 if the county extended its hearings.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax on a Sarpy County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. The documentary stamp tax is $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026, collected by the register of deeds.
